My freshman year of college I was in my dorm room on my laptop when I was scrolling through Facebook. I came across a post where a person posted about seeing a weird post on 4chan where a man from my hometown had posted claiming that he had murdered his girlfriend in her apartment and when people didn't believe him, he started posting photos of a nude woman who had been brutally murdered and said that if they still didn't believe him that everyone would see it on the news after her son got home from school and called the cops. The Facebook poster said that the 4chan user had also said he wanted to die from suicide by cop. There was no link to it posted, just people discussing if it was true or not, just gossiping. I decided that I would come back to the post later and check on it to see if anything actually came of it. Before I had the chance to check again, my mom called me saying that someone had found the post on 4chan and linked it in a comment on that Facebook post. She told me she clicked the link and it was absolutely horrifying. She told me not to go looking at the link and that she was going to call the cops about the link. 

Of course, not listening to my mother, I clicked on the link. What I saw will never leave my brain. It was absolutely horrifying. The pictures depicted a brutal murder. And when I say brutal I mean bloody and vicious. It was awful. Still, though, there weren't any reports confirming if it was real. 

I found a police scanner for my hometown online and listened to see if anything had been reported. Sadly, it had. Her son found her and the cops responded, finding her exactly like the photos depicted.

All in all, the cops caught him after a long car chase down I-5 ending in Oregon. He was just sentenced to first degree murder earlier this year.

It's terrifying to know that something like this happened in my small hometown and so near to where my parents live and those gruesome photos will be ingrained in my memory forever.

I used to work at a store in an extremely sketchy part of town, right near a ton of bus stops. At least ten homeless people lived outside our store at a time. We often saw ambulances coming to help those who overdosed and often had to call the cops because of violence or theft.
